# Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0507a)

**ID:** Atk S0507a
**Section:** Aṭṭhakathā Khuddakanikāya (atk-s05)
**Collection:** Atthakatha-Suttas
**Title (Pali):** Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā
**Title (English, from literature):** Elucidation of the Intrinsic Meaning: The Commentary on the Peta-Stories
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, titled *Paramatthadīpanī*, is the commentary on the *Petavatthu* preserved within the Khuddakanikāya aṭṭhakathā collection [Sayers 2008; Schober 1997]. Traditional scholarship attributes the commentary to Dhammapāla, who is credited with authoring commentaries on seven Khuddakanikāya texts as well as a subcommentary on Buddhaghosa's *Visuddhimagga* [Main 2011; Schober 1997]. The dating of Dhammapāla remains subject to scholarly discussion, with dates proposed in the 6th century or early 7th century CE [Main 2011]. In traditional commentarial relative chronology, it succeeded the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* and the closely related *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [Goonesekere 1967].

Each story in the commentary is structured into three continuous parts: an introductory narrative (*nidāna*) establishing the setting and karmic background of the story, the canonical verses (*gāthā*) themselves, and an exegetical commentary detailing the grammatical, semantic, and doctrinal meaning of the verses [Sayers 2008; Schober 1997]. Along with the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the text functions as a foundational source for Theravāda cosmological and ethical understandings of karmic retribution, rebirth in miserable states (*peta*), and the efficacy of transfer of merit to departed ancestors [Goonesekere 1967; Sayers 2008; Schober 1997]. It also preserves incidental information shedding light on ancient Indian social history, caste communities, and trade guilds [Goonesekere 1967].

According to DharmaNexus, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* shares 22,213 text reuse matches with 314 other Pali texts, showing widespread formulaic and narrative overlap with the commentary literature [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive reuse partners are the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (2,220 matches, longest segment §3216–3235 ↔ §3996–4016), the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* (1,494 matches), several sections of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Khuddakapāṭha-aṭṭhakathā*, and the commentaries on the *Theragāthā* and *Therīgāthā* [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, canonical *Petavatthu* poems such as the *Ambasakkarapetavatthu* (Pv 36) and *Mattāpetivatthu* (Pv 15) exhibit dense textual matches where the verses are embedded within the commentary [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language matches scoring 10 or above [DharmaNexus].

Modern editions include the Sinhalese Hewavitarana edition [Adikaram 1946], a Devanāgarī edition published by the Vipassana Research Institute based on the Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana collection [Main 2011; Shirker 2008], and a digital edition prepared by Muneo Tokunaga for GRETIL [Langer 2007]. An English translation by U Ba Kyaw, edited and annotated by Peter Masefield, was published by the Pali Text Society under the title *Elucidation of the Intrinsic Meaning: The Commentary on the Peta-Stories* [Karashima 2012; Masefield 1979; Shirker 2008].
